note: Hand curation for scripts/build-commentaries.mjs. The deriver reads TITLES, which is a heuristic, not evidence — this file is where its mistakes are corrected and never re-derived. Edit freely; the deriver never writes here.
rule: A work enters the map when its title names a biblical book AND the title either carries a commentary-genre word or governs the book with in/super. The biblical texts THEMSELVES (Liber Genesis, Evangelium secundum Joannem, Psalterium) satisfy neither and are excluded by the rule, not by this list.

addBooks._note: workIdno -> [OSIS] for works the title heuristic gets WRONG or cannot see. Entries here override derivation entirely.

addBooksNotes.3907: Rabanus Maurus, 'Commentaria in Cantica' (PL 112, idno 8930) — NOT the Song of Songs. It expounds the CANTICLES SUNG AT LAUDS, dedicated to King Louis: Isaiah 12, Hezekiah's prayer (Isa 38), Hannah (1 Sam 2), the Song of the Sea (Exod 15), Habakkuk 3, Deuteronomy 32, the Three Children (Dan 3), the Benedictus, the Magnificat and the Nunc dimittis (Luke 1-2). The bare title 'in Cantica' makes the derivation file it under Song of Songs; its own heads name all ten. Found 2026-07-30 when its lemma vocabulary came back almost empty of Song terms and full of Theman, Edom and Anna. THE LESSON: 'Cantica' in a TITLE is not evidence of the Song of Songs — check the heads.

bareCanticaWatch._note: Titles with a BARE 'Cantica/Canticum' (not the doubled 'Cantica canticorum'). The bare form is NOT evidence of the Song of Songs — 8930 Rabanus turned out to expound the ten canticles of Lauds. But it is not always wrong either, so these are not auto-rejected: VERIFY AGAINST THE WORK'S OWN HEADS before translating or trusting the map's placement.
